title: Proof: the positive numerator, and the transport to binding energy
html:
The inequality

Both scalars carry the same denominator q + q^{-1}, which is positive for q > 0, and the ordering therefore reduces to the numerators: \mu_- < \mu_+ is equivalent to q - z < z + q^{-1}, that is to h < 2z with h = q - q^{-1}.

Substituting convention D and clearing denominators turns 2z - h into a closed form rather than an estimate:

  2\,\frac{q^{3}}{q^{2}+1} \;-\; \Bigl(q - \frac1q\Bigr)
  \;=\; \frac{2q^{4} - (q^{2}-1)(q^{2}+1)}{q\,(q^{2}+1)}
  \;=\; \frac{q^{4}+1}{q\,(q^{2}+1)} .

The numerator q^{4}+1 and the denominator q(q^{2}+1) are both strictly positive for q > 0, so 2z - h > 0 identically. Dividing by the common positive denominator restores the inequality on the scalars.

Nothing in the computation is specific to the substrate parameter, and nothing is approximate: the quantity whose sign is at issue has been written as a ratio of positives, which is the strongest form the claim admits.

Transport to binding energy

The binding of a channel is B_T = -\alpha \log \mu_T with \alpha > 0 the energy scale. Since \log is strictly increasing on the positive reals and \mu_- > 0, the inequality \mu_- < \mu_+ gives \log \mu_- < \log \mu_+, and multiplying by -\alpha reverses it:

  B_+ \;=\; -\alpha\log\mu_+ \;<\; -\alpha\log\mu_- \;=\; B_- .

The transport step is where the argument leaves the algebra and enters the archimedean sector, since \log is a real-analytic function and the energy scale is a physical quantity. The inequality it transports, however, was established over an ordered field with no such input, so the two halves of the proof sit on opposite sides of the substrate wall and only the second is specialised.
